name: The Durutti Column
label: Factory Records
lede: Tony Wilson built a punk band around a guitarist from Manchester, the punks left, and Vini Reilly stayed on Factory for the label's whole life, playing guitar that sounded like nothing else on it.

eras.title: A band named after a comic strip
eras.text: Tony Wilson and Alan Erasmus put a band together from the punk group Fast Breeder and a guitarist who had played with Ed Banger and the Nosebleeds. They named it after a Situationist comic and the anarchist militia it was about. Within a year only the guitarist was left.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Durutti Column · Wikipedia: Vini Reilly
years.h: Wilson and Erasmus put the band together around Vini Reilly
years.p: [[Dave Rowbotham|d93c88be-3980-4457-a943-5c368d66277d]] and [[Chris Joyce|d1b0664e-c84c-469d-94e7-ea5a0174b318]] come from Fast Breeder, with [[Tony Bowers|a6d2ce99-64e6-4f62-acf7-3f771122266f]] on bass and [[Vini Reilly|f639c53e-c709-407f-9711-de495461f28d]] on guitar. Phil Rainford sings, then actor Colin Sharp takes over in July.
years.xp:
The name comes from Le Retour de la Colonne Durruti, a 1966 Situationist comic strip, and the Durruti Column militia of the Spanish Civil War.

Reilly had cut his first record with Ed Banger and the Nosebleeds. Wikipedia calls him Wilson's first signing.

years.cap: Ticket for the Durutti Column at the Factory, Russell Club, 1978
years.src: Durutti Column Gigography · Wikipedia: Factory Records
years.h: First gig: the Factory club's opening night at the Russell Club
years.p: The flyer billed it as "The Next Music Begins," with Jilted John and Margox and the Zincs. The club, in an old bus drivers' social club on Royce Road, gave the label its name.

years.h: Two tracks on FAC 2, beside Joy Division
years.p: [[Martin Hannett|ffbfce58-5185-4bcc-8c45-a7cd5d1a3783]] produces the band for Factory's first record, a double 7-inch with [[Joy Division|9a58fda3-f4ed-4080-a3a5-f457aac9fcdd]] and [[Cabaret Voltaire|439a29ad-f4ef-4857-a7cd-3d4a551056c8]].

years.src: Wikipedia: The Durutti Column · Wikipedia: The Mothmen
years.h: The band splits before the album, and Reilly keeps the name
years.p: They fell out over who should produce. Rowbotham, Joyce and Bowers form [[The Mothmen|5c54ad44-fc90-4e90-99d9-e0a5268268cc]]; Joyce and Bowers later play in [[Simply Red|a9100753-f539-43cf-bcc9-579566fb512e]]'s rhythm section from 1984 to 1989.

years.cap: Jon Savage's poster for the Durutti Column at the Lesser Free Trade Hall, December 14, 1979
years.src: Wikipedia: The Return of the Durutti Column · Wikipedia: The Durutti Column
years.h: Hannett and Reilly record at Cargo Studios, Rochdale
years.p: Hannett builds electronic backing tracks and Reilly plays his classical-leaning guitar over them.
years.xp: Reilly on Hannett: "he more or less got sounds for me that no one else could understand."

eras.title: Sandpaper, then a Matisse
eras.text: Factory's packaging got stranger with every Durutti record, and Reilly's music got quieter. The first sleeve was sandpaper; the 1984 one was a Matisse glued onto pulp board.

q: I was completely baffled. 'What, this is really going to be an album?'
years.src: Wikipedia: The Return of the Durutti Column · Wikipedia: The Durutti Column
years.h: The Return of the Durutti Column comes in a sandpaper sleeve
years.p: The first 2,000 copies, an homage to Guy Debord's book Mémoires, were glued together by the band and Joy Division. Early copies came with a flexi of two Hannett pieces.
years.xp:
The sleeve was designed by Rowbotham and Wilson. Later pressings switched to a printed sleeve with Raoul Dufy artwork.

Record Collector later called it "arguably the most distinctive record in the Factory canon."

years.src: Wikipedia: LC · Wikipedia: Bruce Mitchell · Wikipedia: Vini Reilly
years.h: LC, demoed in five hours, recorded in two
years.p: Reilly bought a four-track from [[Bill Nelson|8d463dee-ffae-4028-a3af-ec8ccb595906]], demoed the album in an afternoon, then cut it with drummer [[Bruce Mitchell|c9130b9e-20f2-4d51-805f-833c0c6f2a82]]. The title is the Italian slogan Lotta Continua.
years.xp:
Mitchell, who had played in a trad jazz band around 1960 and in [[Alberto y Lost Trios Paranoias|47373ad3-cd5e-4f00-a300-81bfebbc0e7d]], went on to drum for Reilly and manage the band for the next four decades.

Brian Eno once named LC his favourite album.

years.cap: Vini Reilly on stage at Pandora, 1983
years.p: Reilly and Mitchell's second Factory album together.

years.cap: Matisse's Trivaux Pond on pulp board
years.h: Reilly disowns Without Mercy as Wilson's idea
years.p: Two pieces, 38 minutes, based on Keats's 'La Belle Dame sans Merci' and arranged with [[John Metcalfe|07cf2e3a-bf6a-44b9-9079-842953a671c9]]. Reilly later said it was Wilson's vision, not his.
years.xp: 8vo glued Henri Matisse's Trivaux Pond onto recycled pulp board for the sleeve. The album reached No. 8 on the indie chart and did well in Japan.

eras.title: Morrissey's guitarist, Factory's last
eras.text: Reilly played guitar on a solo No. 1 album and started sampling soul singers on his own records. Then Factory went under.

years.src: Wikipedia: Viva Hate · Wikipedia: Vini Reilly
years.h: Reilly plays on Viva Hate, Morrissey's first solo album
years.p: Producer Stephen Street brings Reilly in on guitars and keyboards. The album goes to No. 1; Reilly then claims he co-wrote almost all of it.
years.xp:
Reilly said he co-composed every track except 'Suedehead'. Street denied it. Years later Reilly took it back: "I have suffered from what they call 'displaced anger'," he said, and called Street "a skilled technician."

Morrissey and Reilly had both been in the Nosebleeds, in different line-ups.

years.h: Otis Redding and Joan Sutherland, looped
years.p: Made with Stephen Street, Vini Reilly builds songs on samples of Otis Redding, Tracy Chapman, Annie Lennox and Joan Sutherland.
years.xp: Early copies came with a bonus single credited to "Vincent Gerard and Steven Patrick", Reilly's and Morrissey's first names.

years.src: Wikipedia: Vini Reilly (album) · Wikipedia: Factory Records
years.h: Obey the Time heads for the dancefloor
years.p: The band's most dance-influenced record is its last on Factory, which collapsed in 1992.

years.h: Dave Rowbotham is found murdered in his Burnage flat
years.p: The founding guitarist was killed with a plasterer's hammer; nobody has been convicted. [[Happy Mondays|01f4fb92-6bf0-4de5-83dc-3fe194e763bf]] wrote a song for him on Yes Please!

eras.title: From the kitchen
eras.text: Wilson died, Reilly had a run of strokes that left him unable to pay the rent, and his fans paid it. Sixteen years after his last record, he made another one at home.

years.h: Tony Wilson dies of complications from kidney cancer, aged 57
years.p: Factory's founder, Reilly's champion since 1978. Reilly's next album, A Paean to Wilson, came out in 2010.

years.h: A stroke takes the feeling from Reilly's left hand
years.p: Reilly starts recording again in February 2011, slower, at the pace his hands allowed.

years.h: Fans send £3,000 in a day and clear Reilly's back rent
years.p: After three strokes and before a disability assessment, Reilly had fallen behind on rent. His nephew made an online appeal over Christmas; the Quietus spread it.
years.xp: His nephew said the donors had "lifted the weight of the world off his shoulders," and that Reilly was determined to rebuild the strength in his hands and play again.

years.p: The first new album since 2010, on London Records, made with Bruce Mitchell and producer Keir Stewart. It tops the UK indie chart.
years.xp: Singer Caoilfhionn Rose sings on two tracks. 'Liars' came out first, on May 27, then 'Scammer'. Metacritic scores it 82.
